sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Brings in the error type, the event rules and the repository. The file states that unknown events and unexpected details are refused and never saved.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps bad or personal data out of the analytics log.

sections.name: track
sections.title: Recording an event
sections.what: Checks an event's name and details against its rules, then saves it. An unknown name or an extra field raises an invalid-input error.
sections.why: Likely reason: only checked data is stored, which matches the rule against free text and personal data.

sections.name: trackOnce
sections.title: Recording a one-time event
sections.what: Records an event only the first time a given user triggers it, such as the first alter ego reveal.
sections.why: Likely reason: the weekly measures count first-time moments, so repeats would inflate them.
sections.watch_out: The code checks first and writes second, so two simultaneous requests can both pass the check.

sections.name: kpisForWeek
sections.title: Weekly summary report
sections.what: Produces the summary for the week containing a chosen day. It uses events up to 44 days after that week's start, or up to now if that is earlier.
sections.why: Likely reason: 44 days covers the week plus the longest retention window, and capping at now avoids counting future data.
sections.watch_out: The reason the KPI module is loaded only when this runs is not stated in the code.

summary: Records product events after checking them, and builds the weekly summary for reports.
purpose: The entry point for saving analytics events and producing weekly numbers.
why: Likely reason: checks keep unknown or personal data out of the analytics log.
how: 1. Find the event's rule. 2. Refuse unknown names. 3. Check the details against the rule. 4. Save the event. For one-time events, check first. For weekly numbers, load history up to 44 days after the week start, capped at now, and pass it to the KPI module.
inputs: An event name, its details, and a user ID or nothing for anonymous events. For weekly numbers, a day and a current time.
outputs: The saved event's ID, nothing for one-time events, or a validation error. A weekly summary.
risks: The one-time check is not atomic, so two simultaneous requests can both save the event.
debug: A refused event shows a message naming the first problem. If weekly numbers look wrong, check the day used and the events loaded.
